stem.text: Determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{\sqrt{n} + 2}{n} \), converges or diverges. Name the test used and verify its conditions.

answer_key.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \ge \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \text{ and } p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The terms are positive, so the direct comparison test applies. Compare with \( \sum \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \), the p-series with \( p = \frac{1}{2} \).
Splitting the fraction, \( \frac{\sqrt{n} + 2}{n} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} + \frac{2}{n} \), so \( \frac{\sqrt{n} + 2}{n} \ge \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} > 0 \) for every n.
The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \ge \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \text{ and } p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \), so \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \) diverges.

options.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \text{ and } p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the comparison inequality written the other way round, which cannot show divergence

options.label: The series converges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0 \).
options.derivation: convergence concluded because the terms approach 0

options.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( a_n \ge \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \text{ and } p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \).
The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( a_n \) decreases to 0.
options.derivation: the alternating series test named for a series of positive terms, its alternating hypothesis never checked
